name: Sortly

mentions.indieAngle: Friends mocked a home inventory app. The business showed up when it moved to small companies.

whyItPrints: Someone asks where the drill is, or how many filters are left. Contractors, schools, and small warehouses pay so the answer is a photo.
whyThisMatters: Someone needs to know where the drill is, or how many filters are left. Sortly is a photo of the thing, with a barcode or a QR code, for tools, supplies, equipment, and stock. It started as a home inventory app. United States. In September 2023 the CEO said on LinkedIn that it had crossed 10 million dollars a year. The climb from 1 million dollars to 10 million dollars took 4.5 years, on 1 million dollars of angel money, and it had been cash-flow neutral for 3 years. More than 30,000 businesses. The figure is self-reported, which means the CEO said it. I did not open the books. Barcodes and QR codes are how a warehouse finds the same item again. The home-inventory start is still the origin story. Schools and small warehouses are named alongside contractors. The angel money is one million dollars, separate from the yearly line.
